basis.title: Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Water-Source Heat Pumps (request for information), 85 FR 27929, May 12, 2020
basis.by: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy
basis.label: equipment lifetime on a retirement function in the form of a Weibull probability distribution, with a mean of 19 years
basis.note: Printed page 27939. Direct match: commercial water-source heat pumps (water-to-air, under 135,000 Btu/h). Value from the July 2015 final rule, restated in this RFI.

basis.title: Updated Buildings Sector Appliance and Equipment Costs and Efficiencies (March 2023), Appendix A: EIA - Technology Forecast Updates - Residential and Commercial Building Technologies - Reference Case (Guidehouse and Leidos, March 3, 2023)
basis.by: U.S. Energy Information Administration; Appendix A prepared by Guidehouse and Leidos
basis.label: Average Life (y) 21 (all years, typical and high efficiency)
basis.note: Printed page 141 (Appendix A). Commercial 4-ton (48 kBtu/h) closed-loop ground-source water-to-air heat pump, the same unit type as a water-source heat pump (DOE regulates both as water-source heat pumps). Data-source sheet (PDF p.241, A-61) gives the life source as 'Guidehouse / Water-Source Unitary Heat Pumps EERE 2015 Final Rule'. That rule (80 FR 42614) used a 19-year mean, so the 21 years is the contractor's figure.

basis.title: Purchasing Energy-Efficient Geothermal Heat Pumps (web page, modified 2026-09-15)
basis.by: U.S. Department of Energy, Federal Energy Management Program
basis.label: Lifetime Energy Cost: The sum of the discounted values of annual energy cost with an average residential geothermal heat pump life of 15 years.
basis.note: Residential geothermal (ground-source) heat pumps, single-phase, open loop, closed loop and direct geoexchange (ENERGY STAR scope). Same water-to-air unit type as a water-source heat pump, but residential; commercial use is not stated. All three tables (Southeast, Southwest, Northern) use 15 years.

open_questions: Every source here is a published planning, design or accounting life. None is observed replacement data.
Written for GSA contracted O&M in US federal buildings; job plans are generic and defer to manufacturer instructions, and the fire extinguisher plans only point to NFPA 10.
